text: Find out what your AI app downloads, or tries to reach, when the network goes away. A common assumption: point the LLM base URL at a local vLLM or Ollama instance and the app is ready for an offline network (an air-gapped VPC, a hospital or defense network, a container with no internet). In practice, many libraries fetch something on first use: tokenizer ranks, ONNX embedding weights, corpora, price maps, or telemetry. Offline, these calls either fail at first use or hang for tens of seconds on retry backoff. None of this is a bug in those libraries. They download once and cache. It only becomes visible when the network is gone. airgap-check tries to surface it before you deploy. Go standard library only. --run requires Docker. # macOS and Linux curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/humanethq/airgap-check/main/install.sh | sh # With Go 1.22+ (also works on Windows) go install github.com/humanethq/airgap-check/cmd/airgap-check@latest # From source git clone https://github.com/humanethq/airgap-check.git cd airgap-check && make build && ./bin/airgap-check --help Usage # static scan airgap-check /path/to/repo # static scan plus a Dockerfile snippet airgap-check --fix /path/to/repo # run in a container with no network airgap-check --run /path/to/repo # use your own image and a smoke test that exercises your code paths airgap-check --run --image my-app:latest --run-cmd " python3 -m pytest tests/smoke_test.py " /path/to/repo # machine-readable output airgap-check --json /path/to/repo Example --fix output (abridged) Read this before applying it: if your app loads Hugging Face models, pre-warm them at build time before setting HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 . Without a warm cache the app fails at startup instead of hanging. # --- BEGIN AIR-GAP & TELEMETRY REMEDIATION --- ENV DO_NOT_TRACK=1 \ NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \ ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=False \ CHROMA_TELEMETRY_IMPL=none \ SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS=true \ HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 \ HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \ TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \ LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=false \ CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true \ OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true \ STREAMLIT_BROWSER_GATHER_USAGE_STATS=false \ XDG_CACHE_HOME=/app/.cache \ TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR=/app/.cache/tiktoken \ HF_HOME=/app/.cache/huggingface \ NLTK_DATA=/app/.cache/nltk_data \ PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/app/.cache/ms-playwright RUN mkdir -p /app/.cache/tiktoken /app/.cache/huggingface /app/.cache/nltk_data /app/.cache/ms-playwright # Pre-warm Python tiktoken encodings at build time RUN TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR=/app/.cache/tiktoken python3 -c "import tiktoken; [tiktoken.get_encoding(e) for e in ('cl100k_base', 'o200k_base')]" # Pre-warm ChromaDB's default ONNX embedding model at build time RUN HOME=/app XDG_CACHE_HOME=/app/.cache python3 -c "from chromadb.utils.embedding_functions import ONNXMiniLM_L6_V2; ef = ONNXMiniLM_L6_V2(); ef(['airgap-warmup'])" # --- END AIR-GAP & TELEMETRY REMEDIATION --- How --run works, and where it stops --run starts a container with --network none , mounts your repository read-only, and mounts a small observer: Limits: We ran airgap-check on 20 open-source Python and TypeScript AI repositories in two phases. Phase 1 (10 repos) was used to find failure modes and tune the rules. Phase 2 (10 repos) is a held-out set: the rules were frozen at commit 8ce2f11 before we ran it. These are probe-based tests: we did not start the applications themselves. Under --network none , we executed probe calls exercising the specific library functions flagged by the static scan (for example, tiktoken.get_encoding('cl100k_base') for gpt-engineer , ChromaDB collection creation and insertion for mem0 and vanna , Hugging Face model resolution for docling and quivr , and a baseline probe for chat-langchain ). Exact probe commands, upstream URLs, and commit SHAs are documented in benchmark/REPOS.md . Times were measured in a container with no network and an immediately refusing DNS sinkhole (see limits above). Browser-side telemetry, such as posthog-js in a frontend bundle, is a separate case: server environment variables do not silence it, because the requests leave from the user's browser. These are probe-based tests: we did not start the applications themselves. A “true positive” means the flagged library fetches something when its call runs offline; it does not prove the repository reaches that call in normal operation. Telemetry findings (for example langsmith, posthog or sentry in several repos) are not scored in the metrics below. At component level: 35 true positives, 4 false positives, 5 false negatives. That is 89.7% precision and 87.5% recall. This is a small sample, so treat the numbers as rough. At repository level, all 9 repositories with first-use downloads were flagged, and chat-langchain was correctly flagged as clean. False positives (all 4): pyproject.toml is scanned as text, so dev and test dependency groups ( playwright in docling , litellm , pydantic-ai ) and an optional extra named posthog triggered warnings. package.json is parsed, so its devDependencies are skipped. False negatives (all 5): OCR weight downloaders ( easyocr , rapidocr , paddleocr ), FlagEmbedding , and LiteLLM's startup fetch of model_prices_and_context_window.json were not in the frozen rule table. --run is meant to catch this kind of miss, but only on the paths it exercises. airgap-check is not a security certification. It reports what it observed; a clean result does not prove that your application is safe to run in an isolated network. Found a library that quietly phones home, or a false positive on your repo? Open an issue with the package name, the call, and the host it tries to reach, and we will add or fix the rule.
